Typing echo and typing interruption are examples of keyboard input. Screen feedback examples are screen echo and progress bar announcement.

object.value: If this check box is selected, the NUM PAD keys and the Extended keys are treated as separate keys rather than as duplicate instances of the same keys. The Extended keys are the keys between the number pad and the main body of the keyboard, and are often referred to as the "six pack" or "inverted T." Once this check box is selected, you can use the check box options in the JAWS Insert Key group Keyboard Manager to assign different commands to these keys. For example, NUM PAD INSERT+UP ARROW and Extended INSERT+UP ARROW could be assigned to separate commands. By default, this check box is cleared.

object.value: Paired keys, which are the LEFT and RIGHT ALT, CTRL, and SHIFT keys, are used interchangeably. For example, if you change a keyboard assignment in Keyboard Manager, and press LEFT CTRL+INSERT+K, when you later activate the command, the LEFT or RIGHT CTRL key can be used as part of the keystroke. You may want to specify to differentiate between these keys when assigning hot keys to make more key combinations available to you. Select this check box to differentiate between the left and right instances of each paired key when making key assignments.   This check box is cleared by default.  This setting is only available in the "Default/All Applications" application.

Paired keys, which are the LEFT and RIGHT ALT, CTRL, and SHIFT keys, are used interchangeably. For example, if you change a keyboard assignment in Keyboard Manager, and press LEFT CTRL+INSERT+K, when you later activate the command, the LEFT or RIGHT CTRL key can be used as part of the keystroke. You may want to specify to differentiate between these keys when assigning hot keys to make more key combinations available to you. Select this check box to differentiate between the left and right instances of each paired key when making key assignments.   This check box is cleared by default.  This setting is only available in the "Default/All Applications" application.

The Key Labels list shows the Key Name, which is the name of the key on the keyboard, the Key Label, which is the label that is echoed when you press the key, and the Mute Status, which indicates whether or not the key label is announced.  Select a Key Name from the list, and choose Toggle Mute to switch between mute and speak status, or choose Change Label to change the key's label.  Press SPACEBAR to open the dialog box.
